I've written `WORK_INSTRUCTIONS.md` for unit 466. It aims at **step 9, criterion 9.7** (HM-REQ-128), not the step 2 the launcher offered.

**Why not step 2:** the plan's own rule R86 (section 6) says steps 2 to 8 can't be worked until 9.4 has a kept change. 9.4 has no route left, because all five techniques 9.3 named are recorded as refused. Of step 9's open lines, 9.7 is the next in section M's order. No unit has tried it, and the loop test found no earlier entry for this approach.

**What the unit does:**
1. **Rules first.** It fixes which metrics count and when the arbitration "loses", before it sees any comparison. It also fixes which decoder is "the better one alone" when the metrics split, and whether the harness or the live path decides.
2. **Three-way table.** It scores the arbitrated transcript, our decoder alone and the fldigi port alone on every metric of sections B and I. It does this per condition, on the harness and on the live path, and writes the result to `docs/phase-requirements/arbitration.md`.
3. **The switch.** It builds a per-condition table that turns arbitration off wherever it loses and uses the better decoder alone. A new test, `TheArbitrationEarnsItsPlaceTests`, names HM-REQ-128 and must be seen failing before it passes.
4. **Exit round.** It ticks 9.7 only if every part is met. It ticks 9.8 only if 9.7 is ticked and the exit checks are green.

**Choices I made myself, each marked in DECIDED as mine and overrulable:**
- **Honesty first.** When the decoders split on metrics, invented characters and sure-but-wrong characters decide before coverage or word boundaries.
- **The live row.** The product live runs only under the "real HF, all" condition, so that row's switch is set from the live measurement.
- **The port alone.** Where HM-REQ-128 names the port as the better decoder on a condition, the port alone is used there, even though HM-REQ-124 gives it no vote. The requirements document takes precedence over the plan, and the report must say what the operator would read in that case.
- **Floor tests.** If a switch would turn a floor test red with a requirement metric worse on that recording, that condition stays on arbitration and 9.7 stays open.

The last report raised items (tie margin, the port retuning live, the leading edge, and others). They're parked or used only to shape the approach. None of them chose the target.

The decision block ends with `ADVANCES: step 9 criterion 7`.

The Gmail, Google Calendar and Google Drive connectors need authorizing in your claude.ai connector settings before they can be used. Nothing here needed them.
